analysis.investment_thesis: Carborundum Universal is a decent Murugappa-group industrial business, but the Magic Formula metrics fail on both legs: earnings yield of ~4.1% (EBIT ₹717 Cr / EV ~₹17,692 Cr) sits well below my 6% floor, and ROCE of 16.1% trails the 20% threshold I require. At 74× earnings for a business whose net profit just dropped 37% year-over-year, the market is pricing in a quality I can't yet see in the numbers.
key_strengths: Diversified abrasives/ceramics/electrominerals portfolio with global reach and nine-year revenue CAGR of 10.8%
Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.08) and strong equity base (₹3,745 Cr) provide balance-sheet resilience for ongoing capex cycle
Murugappa Group stewardship with consistent operational cash flow positive in all 5 of the last 5 years
key_risks: Earnings yield too thin (~4.1%) — stock is priced for perfection at 74× P/E and 32× EV/EBITDA
Net profit collapsed 37% in FY25 (₹299 Cr vs ₹476 Cr in FY24) as other income swung to -₹23 Cr from +₹118 Cr — earnings quality concern
FCF almost zero in FY25 (₹28 Cr) despite ₹304 Cr operating cash flow, absorbed by ₹278 Cr capex — free cash conversion is poor right now
red_flags: Operating margin of only 7.43% for a specialty industrial materials company — structurally thin
EBITDA declined year-over-year (₹805 Cr in FY25 vs ₹864 Cr in FY24) on higher revenue — margin compression
CWIP surged to ₹203 Cr — expanding capex intensity at a time when returns on existing capital are subthreshold
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On the Magic Formula, CARBORUNIV fails both screens simultaneously. Earnings yield = EBIT/EV = ₹717 Cr / ₹17,692 Cr ≈ 4.1%, well below my 6% minimum. ROCE of 16.1% is below the 20% floor I need to call a business 'good.' The combination means the stock is neither cheap nor outstandingly profitable by my rubric. The FY25 profit collapse (₹299 Cr vs ₹476 Cr) amplifies valuation risk — at 74× trailing P/E the market has no margin of safety if earnings disappoint again.

The underlying franchise is solid: abrasives and technical ceramics serve durable industrial end-markets, and the nine-year revenue CAGR of 10.8% is respectable. But the operating margin (7.43%) is too thin for a specialty materials company, and heavy capex is consuming cash flow — FCF in FY25 was just ₹28 Cr against ₹278 Cr of capex. I would revisit if earnings normalise toward ₹450+ Cr and the stock corrects to sub-30× earnings, bringing earnings yield above 6%.
